I. DESCRIPTION OF URBAN RENEWAL PROGRAM
1. General
The Federal Urban Renewal Program was established by the Housing Act of 1949. It consists of loans and graats to assist cities in the removal of blighted and deteriorated areas; the relocation of residents into decent, safe and sanitary housing; the relocation of business firms; the planning for reuse of theland; the rehabilitation of structures that are capable of rehabilitation and which will conform to the land use plan; and the preparation of the cleared land for resale to private redevelopers.
2. The Urban Renewal Process
All actions are carried out by the city or a development agency as authorized by state enabling legislation. To receive Federal assistance in these activities certain criteria and regulations must be met as specified in the Housing Act of 1949 and subsequent Housing Acts. Federal regulations and rules for the program are contained in the Urban Renewal Handbook (RHA 7200 through RHA 7228) as published by the Department of Housing and Urban Development.
The Gross Project Cost consists of all expenditures made by a Local Public Agency (LPA) for a given urban renewal project. The net project cost is the gross cost less proceeds from resale of land. The eligible Federal grant is two thirds of the net project cost (three-quarters for economic development areas as designated by the Department of Commerce and cities under 50,000 population). The local one-third or one-quarter share may be provided in cash or by the provision of certain public improvements or supporting facilities. Up until January 1,1971 relocation assistance was eligible as a 100% Federal grant. It is now shared with the locality at the same ratio as the net project cost.
Upon Federal approval of any initial application, Federal grant funds are reserved and a survey and planning advance is made to complete detailed plans for the project. During this planning period buildings and social needs are surveyed and planning and scheduling are completed. The principal doucument prepared during this period is the Urban Renewal Plan which, when adopted by the local governing body after necessary public hearings, becomes the governing document in regard to acquisition, demolition and rehabilitation. This survey and planning period may last anywhere from one to three years.
After approval of the detailed plans by the local governing body and the Department of Housing and Urban Development the project enters the execution phase.
